title: Nondegenerate bright solitons and their interactions in the generalized coupled nonlinear Schroedinger system
authors: R. Ramakrishnan, Samudra Roy, S. Stalin, M. Lakshmanan
abstract: It is known that the generalized coupled nonlinear Schroedinger (GCNLS) equations can be reduced to the basic vector nonlinear Schroedinger models through various symmetry reductions. By using such reductions, soliton solutions of several interesting types can be obtained for the GCNLS system. In this paper, we show how the non-degenerate soliton solutions can be derived using one such reduction and analyze the various special features associated with the resulting soliton solutions. We find that the obtained non-degenerate soliton solutions exhibit breathing behavior, characterized by a breathing frequency. We also show that the vector solitons emerging from the reduction undergo elastic collisions with the standard phase shift, similar to the non-degenerate solitons of other coupled nonlinear Schroedinger models. Further, they undergo interesting energysharing collisions when they interact with the already known bright solitons. These collision scenarios are further confirmed by an appropriate asymptotic analysis. We have also analyzed the stability of the obtained vector solitons and found that they are stable against random perturbations. The results presented here enhance the understanding of the nature and dynamics of non-degenerate vector solitons.
summary: This paper analyzes nondegenerate bright solitons within the GCNLS system, demonstrating that these solutions exhibit characteristic breathing behavior. The authors characterize their collision dynamics—showing both elastic and energy-sharing interactions—and confirm their stability against random noise perturbations using advanced analytical and numerical methods.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature, dynamics, and interactions of nondegenerate bright solitons within the Generalized Coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger (GCNLS) system.
main_result: The derived non-degenerate vector solitons exhibit breathing behavior, undergo elastic collisions with standard phase shifts, and are shown to be stable against random perturbations.
method: The research employs analytical techniques including linear transformations from known integrable models, asymptotic analysis for collision dynamics, and numerical stability testing using Gaussian white noise.
model_or_system: The system is governed by the GCNLS equations, which incorporate self-phase modulation, cross-phase modulation, and four-wave mixing effects. It is treated as a completely integrable dynamical system.
key_observables: Breathing frequency, collision dynamics (elastic vs. energy-sharing), stability against noise, and soliton profile shape preservation/change.
important_parameters: Linear coupling parameters ($\alpha_j$), four-wave mixing parameter ($b$), relative velocity ($\Delta v$), and the level of added Gaussian white noise (3% and 5%).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific symmetry reductions and linear transformations connecting GCNLS to Manakov-type models; stability is tested against specified levels of random perturbations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate double-hump nondegenerate vector solitons (Fig. 1), breathing behavior (Fig. 2), collision structures for different velocity regimes (Figs. 4, 7), and numerical confirmation of stability under noise addition (Fig. 10).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the GCNLS model and derives non-degenerate solutions via reduction to a Manakov-type system. It then analyzes the breathing nature and collision dynamics using asymptotic methods, concluding with rigorous stability analysis against random perturbations.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed insights into complex nonlinear wave phenomena in coupled systems, which is highly relevant for understanding light propagation in optical fibers or Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) modeled by NLS equations.
